title: ReplaySSM Speeds GLM and Kimi Inference Up to 2.1x in Production
summary:
A new computational method for State Space Models is now live across various AI models and deployment frameworks. The ReplaySSM technique is active in GLM-5.3-Flash and Kimi-K3, and has been integrated into vLLM, TensorRT-LLM, SGLang, and FlashInfer. The update increases the speed of standard decoding by up to 1.47x and speculative decoding by up to 2.1x, while enabling a low-precision state that prevents rounding errors from propagating through recurrence.

Developed in collaboration with Nvidia, the method caches State Space Model (SSM) inputs instead of the state to separate output computation from state updates during decoding. This approach gives SSMs access to inference optimizations typically reserved for Transformers, such as quantization and speculative decoding. The researchers stated the performance gains result from an IO-aware memory strategy similar to the logic used in Mamba scan, paged KV, and FlashAttention.

selectedTweets.text:
ReplaySSM now runs in production in GLM-5.3-Flash and Kimi-K3, and ships in TensorRT-LLM, vLLM, FlashInfer, and SGLang!

It speeds up standard decoding (up to 1.47x) and speculative decoding (up to 2.1x), and now also enables a low-precision SSM state whose rounding error never propagates through the recurrence.

Building on our earlier ReplaySSM work, we collaborated with @NVIDIA to pin down what the method really unlocks. Caching SSM inputs instead of the state is what ReplaySSM does. What it changes is that computing the output and updating the state can be separated during decoding. All three gains follow from that separation.

Joint blog post, paper, and code with @NVIDIA and @tri_dao 👇
